facts.statement: Xuwulong is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Yujingzi Basin in Gansu Province, northwestern China.
facts.quote: Xuwulong is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of what is now Yujingzi Basin in the Jiuquan area, Gansu Province of northwestern China.

facts.statement: The species is known from a single articulated holotype specimen (GSGM F00001) containing a complete skull, nearly complete spine, and full left pelvis from the Xinminbao Group.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype, GSGM F00001, an articulated specimen including a complete cranium, almost complete axial skeleton, and complete left pelvic girdle recovered from the Xinminbao Group.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Liu Weichang in 2011.
facts.quote: Xuwulong was named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Liu Weichang in 2011

facts.statement: The type species is Xuwulong yueluni, a name honoring Professor Wang Yue-lun.
facts.quote: the type species is Xuwulong yueluni; the binomial name as a whole refers to Professor Wang Yue-lun

facts.statement: The holotype specimen GSGM-F00001 was formally described as the new taxon Xuwulong yueluni in 2011.
facts.quote: This specimen, now in the Gansu Geological Museum as GSGM-F00001, was then described in 2011 by You, Li, and Liu Weichang as the holotype of the new taxon Xuwulong yueluni.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence places Xuwulong in the upper Aptian stage of the Xiagou Formation.
facts.quote: Xuwulong can be placed in the upper Aptian in the Xiagou Formation through these correlations.

facts.statement: Xuwulong belongs to the parent group Hadrosauroidea.
Xuwulong is classified within the class Ornithischia.
Xuwulong lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Sediments from the Yujingzi Basin are correlated to the Paquier Event, an ocean anoxic event spanning the late Aptian to early Albian.
rejected.quote: Carbon isotopes from the Yujingzi Basin sediments show sediments of the area are correlated to the ocean anoxic event named the Paquier Event, spanning the late Aptian to early Albian.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'event spanning the late Aptian to early Albian'
